chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad al-Wasiti, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed Ibrahim (peace be upon him) complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about what he faced from the bad character of Sarah. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed to him: "Indeed, the example of the woman is the example of the crooked rib. If you straighten it, you break it, and if you leave it, you enjoy with it. Be patient with her."'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor of the crooked rib in the context of marital relations?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) utilizes the metaphor of the 'crooked rib' (al-dal' al-mu'ajaj) to advise Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) on marital patience, emphasizing that forcing a spouse to conform rigidly to one's expectations leads to fracture, whereas acceptance fosters harmony. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the concept of 'uyub' (quirks/flaws) in spouses, distinguishing between inherent nature and correctable behavior, and underscores the virtue of sabr (patience) as a practical remedy for domestic discord.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Al Wasity who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> complained to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic from what he<sup>as</sup> faced from the evil manners of Sarah<sup>as</sup>. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “But rather, and example of the woman is the example of the crooked rib. If you<sup>as</sup> were to straighten it, you will break it, but if you were to leave it (as it is), you<sup>as</sup> will enjoy with it. Be patient upon her”’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban al-Ahmar from Muhammad al-Wasitiy who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam once complained before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, because of the wicked moral behavior of Sarah and Allah most High, sent him revelation that said, ‘Women are like crooked ribs, on trying to straighten you only cause it to snap and break apart but you can benefit by leaving it alone (the way it is), so you must exercise patience.’”
